observations.text: SP flew the ELP after the IP's command, but did not carry the pattern to the aim point without assistance, and the IP directed the turn to low key and made part of the control inputs on the final glide. Altitude at high key was 350 feet above the briefed value and airspeed on the base key leg was 18 knots above the target, while the simulated touchdown point fell beyond the first 1/3 of the RWY. Performance is within the standards expected for this stage, however it sits at the lower edge of them, since IP direction was required at every key point and not only for the sequencing. Study of the ELP key point altitudes and of the configuration schedule is expected to reduce the level of direction needed on the next sortie.

SP flew the ELP to a touch and go, making all control inputs personally and needing only the IP's verbal prompts on the sequence of the key points, without any intervention on the controls. The A/C was configured timely and correctly after prompting, and no stall characteristics that could lead to advancing the throttle were allowed to appear. Deviations reached 15 knots above the target airspeed and 300 feet above the briefed low key altitude, and were recognized and corrected with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and flew the ELP without the IP's verbal prompts or intervention, configuring the A/C timely and correctly at each key point. Minor errors in the judgement of the turn to base key produced deviations of 12 knots above the target airspeed and 220 feet above the briefed key point altitude, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner. The simulated touchdown was placed within the first 1/3 of the RWY and no stall characteristics appeared. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the ELP in order to touch within the first 1/3 of the RWY and flew it promptly and accurately, configuring the A/C timely and correctly and stating the engine restart procedure in simulation. Airspeed never exceeded the target by more than 8 knots nor fell more than 4 knots below it, and altitude at the key points was held within 120 feet of the briefed values. No stall characteristics were allowed to appear and the pattern was closed with a touch and go as briefed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and flew the ELP from the IP's command without hesitation, placing the simulated touchdown in the first third of the RWY and configuring the A/C timely and correctly at every key point. Airspeed was held within 3 knots of the target throughout the glide and altitude at high key, low key and base key was within 40 feet of the briefed values. The engine restart procedure was stated and executed in simulation without prompting, no stall characteristics appeared, and the pattern was closed with a touch and go as briefed. Accuracy and speed of execution were above the level expected of a student at this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late and non-standardized configuration schedule, did not lower the gear and the flaps at the briefed key points and could not complete the ELP without assistance. The IP directed the corrections and made part of the control inputs on the final glide, with the result that the A/C arrived at base key 340 feet low and 14 knots below the target airspeed, and the simulated touchdown point fell short of the RWY threshold. Review of the ELP configuration schedule against the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required before the item is repeated.

SP, due to surprise at the unannounced simulated malfunction, which delayed the first control input, did not establish the glide airspeed nor turn toward high key within the time available. The IP had to direct the entry and fly part of the pattern, with the result that the A/C passed low key 380 feet below the briefed altitude and 17 knots above the target airspeed, and the approach was closed with a Go Around directed by the IP. Immediate recognition of the condition and establishment of the glide are required before the item is repeated.

SP flew the ELP to a touch and go, making all control inputs personally and completing the pattern with the IP's verbal prompts on the configuration and on the turn to base key, without intervention on the controls. Airspeed reached 15 knots above the target on the descent to low key and altitude at the key points reached 300 feet above the briefed values, the errors being recognized and corrected with delay. Performance is within the standards expected for this stage, however it sits at the upper edge of them, since the deviations reached the limit of the acceptable band. Anticipation of the configuration points is expected to reduce both the prompting and the size of the deviations on the next sortie.

SP planned and flew the ELP without the IP's verbal prompts or intervention, configuring the A/C timely and correctly and placing the simulated touchdown within the first 1/3 of the RWY. Minor errors in the management of the glide inside the turn to base key produced 13 knots above the target airspeed and 210 feet above the briefed key point altitude, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner. No stall characteristics were allowed to appear and the pattern was closed with a touch and go. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the ELP in order to touch within the first 1/3 of the RWY and flew it promptly and accurately after the IP's command, without prompting or intervention. The A/C was configured timely and correctly at each key point, the engine restart procedure was stated and executed in simulation, and no stall characteristics were allowed to appear. Airspeed never exceeded the target by more than 7 knots nor fell more than 4 knots below it, and altitude at high key, low key and base key was held within 110 feet of the briefed values. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ELP from the IP's command with no hesitation and no prompting, planning the pattern so that the simulated touchdown fell in the first third of the RWY on every attempt. Configuration was timely and correct at each key point, the engine restart procedure was executed in simulation without being called for, and no stall characteristics appeared at any stage. Airspeed was held within 2 knots of the target and altitude at the key points within 40 feet of the briefed values. Accuracy and speed of execution were above the level expected of a student at this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect assessment of the wind effect on the glide, did not adjust the ground track between high key and low key and could not complete the ELP without assistance. The IP directed the pattern from low key onward and made part of the control inputs, with the result that the A/C reached base key 360 feet below the briefed altitude and 13 knots below the target airspeed, and the simulated touchdown point fell short of the first 1/3 of the RWY. Review of the ELP wind correction technique in the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required before the item is repeated.

SP, due to absorption in the cockpit indications of the simulated malfunction, which left the descent rate unmonitored, did not fly the briefed key point altitudes and did not configure the A/C at the planned points. The IP directed the configuration and executed part of the final glide, with the result that the A/C crossed low key 420 feet high and 19 knots above the target airspeed, and the approach was closed with a Go Around. Flying the A/C first and working the simulated malfunction second is required before the item is repeated.

SP, due to a non-standardized turn to base key flown with excessive bank, did not hold the planned glide profile and re-established it only after the IP's verbal prompts. The corrections were applied with delay and without intervention on the controls, with the result that airspeed reached 15 knots above the target and the A/C arrived at base key 300 feet above the briefed altitude. The pattern was closed with a Go Around and no stall characteristics were allowed to appear.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn to low key, did not configure the A/C timely and did not check the key point altitude before rolling out. The ELP was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts on the configuration and on the aim point, the errors being recognized and corrected with delay, with the result that airspeed fell 10 knots below the target and the A/C passed base key 200 feet below the briefed altitude. The simulated touchdown point fell beyond the first 1/3 of the RWY and the pattern was closed with a touch and go.

SP planned and flew the ELP within the desired standards, configuring the A/C timely and correctly and closing the pattern with a touch and go without IP's intervention. However, the aim point was reassessed twice between low key and base key, and airspeed reached 13 knots above the target while altitude at base key reached 230 feet above the briefed value, both deviations recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - these values sit near the outer edge of the acceptable band, and a firmer aim point selection at low key is expected to reduce them on the next sortie.

SP planned the ELP in order to touch within the first 1/3 of the RWY and flew it promptly and accurately, without prompting or intervention. The A/C was configured timely and correctly at each key point, the engine restart procedure was stated and executed in simulation, and no stall characteristics that could lead to advancing the throttle were allowed to appear. Airspeed never exceeded the target by more than 8 knots nor fell more than 4 knots below it, and altitude at high key, low key and base key was held within 130 feet of the briefed values. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ELP from the IP's command without hesitation, planning the pattern so that the simulated touchdown fell in the first third of the RWY and correcting the ground track for the wind without prompting. Configuration was timely and correct at every key point and the engine restart procedure was executed in simulation as part of the flow. Airspeed was held within 3 knots of the target throughout the glide and altitude at high key, low key and base key within 35 feet of the briefed values, with no stall characteristics at any stage. Accuracy and speed of execution were above the level expected of a student at this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an ELP entry flown without first trimming for the glide airspeed, did not arrive at high key on the briefed altitude and could not complete the pattern without assistance. The IP directed the sequence from high key onward and made part of the control inputs, with the result that the A/C crossed low key 330 feet below the briefed altitude and 16 knots above the target airspeed, and the approach was closed with a Go Around directed by the IP. Establishment and trimming of the glide airspeed before entering the pattern are required before the item is repeated.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published engine restart procedure for the condition presented, did not state or execute it in simulation and did not carry the ELP to the aim point without assistance. The IP directed both the restart sequence and the configuration and executed part of the final glide, with the result that airspeed fell 16 knots below the target inside the turn to base key and the A/C arrived 250 feet below the briefed base key altitude. Further study of the engine restart procedure is required before the item is repeated.

SP, due to a configuration schedule applied later than the briefed key points, did not maintain the planned glide profile and completed the ELP only after the IP's verbal prompts on the gear, the flaps and the aim point. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay and without intervention on the controls, with the result that airspeed reached 15 knots above the target on the descent and the A/C passed base key 300 feet above the briefed altitude. The simulated touchdown point fell beyond the first 1/3 of the RWY and the pattern was closed with a touch and go.

SP, due to a failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not check the airspeed against the target once the gear and the flaps were extended. The ELP was completed after the IP's verbal prompts, with recognition and correction applied with delay and with no intervention on the controls, the result being that airspeed fell 10 knots below the target in the turn to base key and the A/C reached the key point 200 feet below the briefed altitude. No stall characteristics were allowed to appear and the pattern was closed with a Go Around.

SP, due to a shallow bank in the turn from low key to base key, did not hold the planned ground track and drifted wide of the aim point. The deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, with the result that airspeed reached 13 knots above the target and the A/C arrived at base key 220 feet above the briefed altitude, the simulated touchdown remaining within the first 1/3 of the RWY. Configuration was timely and correct and no stall characteristics appeared.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the final glide, did not cross-check the airspeed against the target through the last part of the pattern. The error was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, with the result that airspeed fell 8 knots below the target and the A/C descended 190 feet below the briefed base key altitude. The engine restart procedure had been stated and executed in simulation and the pattern was closed with a touch and go as briefed.

SP planned the ELP in order to touch within the first 1/3 of the RWY and flew it accurately and without IP's intervention, configuring the A/C timely and correctly at each key point. However, the aim point required a second assessment at low key, and airspeed reached 9 knots above the target while altitude at base key reached 140 feet above the briefed value. Marginal performance for the Training Section - these values sit near the outer edge of the desired band, and an earlier aim point decision at low key is expected to consolidate the margin on the next sortie.

SP flew the ELP from the IP's command without hesitation and without prompting, planning the pattern so that the simulated touchdown fell in the first third of the RWY on every attempt. Configuration was timely and correct at every key point, the engine restart procedure was stated and executed in simulation as part of the flow, and no stall characteristics that could lead to advancing the throttle appeared at any stage. Airspeed was held within 2 knots of the target throughout the glide and altitude at high key, low key and base key within 30 feet of the briefed values. Accuracy and speed of execution were above the level expected of a student at this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.
